q1005:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Onomatopiea** — iski sahi spelling **Onomatopoeia** hai; baaki teeno (Apothegm, Esoterica, Sesquipedalian) sahi spellding hain.

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Spelling — Greek-origin words mein vowel sequence (P-O-E-I-A) waise hi rehti hai, "sound ke hisaab se" likhne se galat ho jaati hai.**

Yahan koi grammar rule nahi, **Vocabulary / Spelling** ka rule hai. Greek loanwords English mein aate hain to unka vowel-cluster original Greek se aata hai, aur pronunciation se spelling ka andaza lagana khatarnaak hota hai.

Is question mein words par ishara karo:
- **A-po-thegm** → Greek *apo* + *thegma*, vowel order theek hai. ✔
- **Eso-te-ri-ca** → Greek *esoterikos* se, "eso" + "terica" theek. ✔
- **Onomato-piea** → yahi trap hai. Bola jaata hai "onomato-**pee**-ya", isliye dimag "piea" likh deta hai. Lekin original Greek **onoma** (naam) + **poiein** (banana) se bana hai → **onomato + poeia** = **Onomatopoeia**. Yani **p-o-e-i-a**, "p-i-e-a" nahi. ✘
- **Ses-qui-pe-da-li-an** → Latin *sesqui* (one-and-a-half) + *pes* (foot), spelling theek. ✔

**Yahi ek-letter ka farq** is poore question ka jawab hai: `poeia` vs `piea`.

> ⚠️ Chhota note: *Apothegm* ka ek British variant *apophthegm* bhi hota hai, par *apothegm* bilkul valid aur standard spelling hai — isliye woh galat nahi hai.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **Apothegm** — ✔ Sahi. *Apo-thegm*, matlab "sankhep mein kahi gayi neetipurn baat" (a terse saying). Spelling valid.
- **Esoterica** — ✔ Sahi. *Eso* (andar) + *terica*, matlab "sirf khaas logon ko samajh aane wali cheezein". Spelling valid.
- **Onomatopiea** — ✘ **GALAT**. Sahi = **Onomatopoeia**. "-piea" nahi, "-poeia" hoga. Yahi answer hai.
- **Sesquipedalian** — ✔ Sahi. *Sesqui* (1.5) + *ped* (foot), matlab "lambi-lambi words use karne wala". Spelling valid.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**Spelling rule ka core:** Greek/Latin origin ke lambe words mein **vowel-cluster ko todna nahi hai** — usse waisa hi likho jaisa root mein hai.

**Onomatopoeia ko todo:**
$$\text{Onoma (नाम)} + \text{poiein (बनाना)} = \text{Onomatopoeia}$$
- Meaning: **dhwani-anukaran** — jaisi awaaz, waisa shabd (buzz, hiss, cuckoo, splash).
- Letters: O-N-O-M-A-T-O-P-**O-E-I-A** → total **11 letters**.
- Dhyan do: **"poe"** = 3 letters (p, o, e), uske baad "ia". Beech mein **"i" nahi** aata "poe" se pehle.

**Isi family ke words (spelling ek hi rehti hai):**
- ✔ Onomatopoeia → ✘ Onomatopiea, Onomatopeia, Onomatopeea
- ✔ Onomatopoeic (adjective) → ✘ Onomatopieic
- ✔ Onomatopoeically (adverb)
- ✔ Onomatopoetic (alternate adjective) — ye bhi valid hai

**Aur 5 examples jahan "pronunciation ≠ spelling" trap banta hai:**

| ✔ Sahi | ✘ Galat (common) | Kyun galat |
|---|---|---|
| **Onomatopoeia** | Onomatopiea | Greek *poiein* |
| **Diarrhoea** | Diarrhiea | Greek *rhein* (behna) |
| **Anaemia** | Aniemia | Greek *haima* (khoon) |
| **Archaeology** | Archiology | Greek *archaios* (purana) |
| **Paediatrician** | Piediatrician | Greek *pais/pedos* (bachcha) |
| **Pharaoh** | Pharoah | — |

**Sentence mein usage:**
- ✔ *"Buzz", "hiss" aur "splash" **onomatopoeic** words hain.*
- ✔ *Poet ne **onomatopoeia** ka khoob use kiya — "the murmuring of innumerable bees".*
- ✘ *Poet ne **onomatopiea** ka use kiya.* (galat spelling)

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
SSC (CGL/CHSL/CPO) mein **"Identify the misspelt word"** ka poora topic in rules par ghoomta hai:

1. **Double consonant trap** — *accommodation, committee, occurrence*. ✘ *acommodation, commitee*
2. **"ie" vs "ei"** — i-before-e except after c: *believe, receive, ceiling, achieve*. ✘ *beleive, recieve*
3. **Silent-letter words** — *rhythm, psalm, debt, muscle, doubt*. ✘ *rythm, rythm, debt*
4. **Greek "ph" = f sound** — *philanthropy, phenomenon, philosophy*. ✘ *philosphy*
5. **"ance/ence" aur "ant/ent" endings** — *maintenance, occurrence, independent, persistence*. ✘ *maintainance, independant*
6. **"ary/ery/ory" endings** — *February, stationary (fixed) vs stationery (pen-paper), mandatory*. ✘ *Febuary*
7. **British vs American trap** — *colour/color, centre/center* — SSC mein in dono ko aksar galat nahi mana jaata, isliye sirf *actual* misspelling dhoondo.
8. **Long academic words (jinke root Greek/Latin hain)** — *sesquipedalian, esoterica, apothegm, ubiquitous, quintessential* — inme ek vowel badal kar option banate hain.
9. **"ough" family** — *thorough, borough, thoroughfare*. ✘ *thourough*
10. **Words with "rr" / "ss" / "ll"** — *embarrass, occurrence, fulfil/fulfill, success*. ✘ *embarass, sucess*

**Trap ka pattern:** SSC hamesha **ek hi letter** badalta hai — vowel ya double letter — taaki word "padhne mein theek" lagee. Isliye **har word ko zor se, syllable-by-syllable todkar padho** (o-no-ma-to-poe-i-a), sirf aankh se mat dekho.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
> **"Onomato + POE + ia"** — is word ke andar chhupa hai *Edgar Allan **Poe*** ka naam!
> **Poe** likhne ke baad hi **-ia** aata hai: **Onomato + POE + ia**.
> Yaad rakho: **"Poe" ke andar 'o' pehle, 'e' baad mein.** "Pie" (cake) ke chakkar mein mat padho — ye **POE** hai, **PIE** nahi. 🥧❌

Poe → onomato**poe**ia. Bas.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**Onomatopoeia = onomato + POE + ia; "PIE" nahi "POE" — isliye "Onomatopiea" galat aur baaki teeno options sahi hain.**
q1006:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Myocardial** — yehi correct adjective hai jo heart ki muscular tissue (myocardium) se related hone ka matlab deta hai.

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Vocabulary / Spelling — Suffix & Root-Word Rule (Greek-Latin medical root + noun→adjective suffix).**

Is sentence mein adjective maanga gaya hai jo "the muscular tissue of the heart" ko darshata hai. Yahan root word banta hai **myocardium** (myo = muscle + cardium = heart). Rule ye hai: noun jab **-ium** par khatam ho aur usse adjective banana ho, to **-ium → -ial** ho jaata hai (yaani `-al` suffix add hota hai, aur `-um` hat jaata hai).

Isliye:
- myocard**ium** → myocard**ial** ✔

Dekho words ki taraf: root **myocardi-** (fix rehta hai) + suffix **-al** (adjective banane wala, jaise *cardium → cardiac* ke pattern mein bhi -ac/-al family ka kaam hota hai). Options mein confusion sirf last 2–3 letters ka hai: **-ac / -ial / -iol / -ial**. Sahi tail **-ial** hai.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **Myocardiac** ✘ — `-ac` suffix laga diya, par heart-muscle ke liye standard adjective "myocardial" hai, "myocardiac" medical dictionaries mein accepted spelling nahi hai (aur ye "cardiac"-style ending ko galat jagah copy karta hai).
- **Myocordial** ✘ — beech mein **o** aa gaya (`myocord-`), jabki root **myocardi-** hai (a-n-kram: m-y-o-c-a-r-d-i). Spelling hi bigad gayi.
- **Myocardial** ✔ — root **myocardi-** + adjective suffix **-al** = bilkul standard form. Jaise *myocardial infarction* (heart attack) likha jaata hai.
- **Myocardiol** ✘ — **-iol** ending nonsensical hai; aisa koi English adjective nahi hai. Di-/-ol endings "myocardial" mein kabhi nahi aate.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**Meaning:** *Myocardial* = relating to the **myocardium**, yaani heart ki wo muscular (mascular) wall jiske saath heart ka contraction hota hai.

**Root breakdown:**
- **myo-** (Greek *mys*) = muscle
- **cardi-** (Greek *kardia*) = heart
- **-ium** = noun-ending (tissue/organ ke liye, jaise *myocardium*)
- **-al** = adjective banane wala suffix (relating to waale matlab ke liye)

**Family patterns (yaad rakhne ke liye):**
| Noun (tissue/organ) | Adjective (-al / -ac) |
|---|---|
| myocardium | myocardial |
| endocardium | endocardial |
| pericardium | pericardial |
| epicardium | epicardial |
| heart (general) | cardiac |

**Examples (✔ sahi vs ✘ galat):**
1. ✔ He suffered a **myocardial** infarction last year. / ✘ … a myocardiac infarction.
2. ✔ **Myocardial** tissue needs continuous oxygen. / ✘ Myocordial tissue needs…
3. ✔ The ECG showed **myocardial** damage. / ✘ The ECG showed myocardial damage. *(wahi sentence, sirf -iol galat hai)*
4. ✔ **Cardiac** arrest aur **myocardial** infarction do alag cheezein hain. / ✘ Myocardiac arrest.

**Exception/care:** *Cardiac* (heart se related, general) aur *myocardial* (heart ki muscle se related, specific) me confuse mat hona. Dono sahi hain, par context decide karta hai. Aur dhyan do — "-ium" waale medical nouns ka adjective almost always **-ial** hota hai, **-ium → -ac** nahi.

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
SSC CGL/CHSL/CPO mein spelling + word-formation ke ye traps baar-baar aate hain:

1. **Medical root + suffix:** myocardium→**myocardial**, endocardium→**endocardial**, bacterium→**bacterial** (bacteriac ✘).
2. **-ary vs -ery** trap: *stationary* (still) vs *stationery* (writing material).
3. **-ance vs -ence**: *maintenance*, *occurrence*, *perseverance* — silent-letter traps.
4. **-able vs -ible**: *eligible, sensible, permissible* vs *adorable, suitable*.
5. **Double consonant trap**: *embarrass*, *accommodation*, *committee*, *recommend*.
6. **Silent initial letter**: *pneumonia*, *psychology*, *knack* — SSC misspelling option isi par banata hai.
7. **-ous vs -ious**: *famous* vs *religious, ambitious*.
8. **Same-sound different-meaning (homophone)**: *complement/compliment*, *principal/principle*, *practical/practicable*.

Trick: SSC options banaata hai **ek letter badal kar** (a/o/i / extra vowel). Isliye spelling question mein poora word loud padho aur syllable-by-syllo check karo: **my-o-car-di-al**.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"MYO (muscle) + CARDI (heart) + AL (adjective)"** → **MyoCARDIal**. Beech mein **"CARDI"** ko pakad lo (jaise *CARDIac* mein hai) — `myo` + `cardi` + `al`. Aur **-ium wale organ ka -ial** yaad rakho: *pericardium→pericardial, myocardium→myocardial*. "Myocordial" aur "Myocardiol" dono mein **'o'/'i' ka ghapala** hai — inhe hamesha galat maano.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**Myo (muscle) + cardi (heart) + al (adjective) = Myocardial — heart ki muscle se related; baaki teen options spelling ke jaal hain.**
q1007:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Glossophobia** — kyunki "glosso" ka matlab hai tongue/jeevh aur public speaking mein jeevh (bolne ki kriya) hi kaam aati hai, isliye *fear of public speaking* = Glossophobia.

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: One-Word Substitution (Greek root "phobia" wali vocabulary)**.
Yahan sentence ke words ko dekho — *"Fear of public speaking"*. Ye ek "phobia" (dar) hai, aur SSC mein har phobia ka ek fixed Greek/Latin root hota hai jo us dar ki **khaas cheez** ko batata hai. Yani koi bhi "-phobia" option chalega nahi — root ko match karna padega.

Sentence ka *"public speaking"* = **tongue / zubaan se bolna** → Greek mein "tongue" = *glōssa* → isliye **Glossophobia**.

> ⚠️ Trap: Har "-phobia" dar batata hai, par kaunsa dar — ye uske **root word** se decide hota hai. Root hi asli answer hai.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **Glossophobia** ✔ — *glosso* = tongue/jeevh → **bolne ka dar / public speaking ka dar**. Yahi question chah raha hai.
- **Sociophobia** ✘ — *socio* = society/log → **logon ke saath milne-julne ya social gatherings ka dar**. Ye public *speaking* se alag hai; ye "stage pe bolne" nahi, "samaaj mein ghusne" ka dar hai.
- **Anthophobia** ✘ — *antho* = flower (jaise *anthology* = phoolon ka sangrah) → **phoolon ka dar**. Public speaking se koi lena-dena nahi.
- **Ergophobia** ✘ — *ergo* = work/kaam (jaise *energy*, *ergonomics*) → **kaam karne ka dar**. Isse bolne se koi rishta nahi.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**-phobia** = kisi cheez ka **abnormal/intense dar**. Root + phobia mila kar naya word banta hai. SSC ise *One-Word Substitution* ke section mein puchta hai — socha jaye to bilkul **combine-and-match** hai.

**Common roots jo yaad rakhne hain:**

| Root | Matlab | Word | Ka Dar |
|---|---|---|---|
| glosso | tongue | Glossophobia | public speaking |
| socio | society | Sociophobia | logon ka / social gatherings |
| anthropo | human | Anthropophobia | insaanon ka |
| anthropo | human | **Acrophobia** (acro = height) | unchai ka |
| claustro | closed place | Claustrophobia | band/closed jagah ka |
| acro | height | Acrophobia | unchai ka |
| agora | open/public place | Agoraphobia | khuli bheed wali jagah ka |
| hydropho | water | Hydrophobia | paani ka |
| nycto | night | Nyctophobia | raat/andhere ka |
| xen(o) | foreigner/stranger | Xenophobia | ajnabiyon ka |
| ergo | work | Ergophobia | kaam ka |
| antho | flower | Anthophobia | phoolon ka |

**Examples (✔ sahi vs ✘ galat):**
- ✔ *She avoids the stage — she has **glossophobia**.*
- ✘ *She avoids the stage — she has **anthophobia**.* (ye flower ka dar hai, stage ka nahi)
- ✔ *Her **claustrophobia** makes lifts unbearable.*
- ✘ *Her **hydrophobia** makes lifts unbearable.* (hydrophobia ~ rabies/paani ka dar)
- ✔ *He fears crowds: **agoraphobia**.*
- ✘ *He fears crowds: **ergophobia**.* (wo kaam ka dar hai)

**Agar "fear" ke bajaye "person" poocha jaye** to *-phobic* ya *-phobe* aata hai — jaise *xenophobe* = ajnabiyon se darne wala.

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **-phobia + root matching** — "fear of water" aaye to *Hydrophobia*, "fear of height" aaye to *Acrophobia*. Root pakdo, pura word apne aap ban jayega.
2. **-philia (love/pasand wala dar ka ulta)** — *hydrophilia* = paani ki pasand.
3. **-logy vs -phobia confusion** — *phonology* (awaaz ka science) vs *phonophobia* (awaaz ka dar). Science wala suffix alag hai.
4. **-cide (killing)** — *patricide* = baap ko maarna; SSC isse "fear" ke saath mix karke trap banata hai.
5. **-mancy (jadui/vidya)** — *necromancy* = murdon se baat karne ki vidya.
6. **-graphy (likhna/record)** — *biography*, *calligraphy*.
7. **-archy / -cracy (shasan)** — *monarchy* (ek raja ka), *democracy* (janata ka). "Rule by few" = *Oligarchy*.
8. **Trap:** *Anthophobia* (phool) aur *Anthropophobia* (insaan) — spelling ka ek hi extra 'p' matlab badal deta hai. Dono options saath aayein to *root* padho: *antho* vs *anthropo*.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"Glo-SSO" → "Glo" se "gala"!** Gala (tongue) = bolna = public speaking.
Aur *"Socio" mein soch"* — *social* bhool jao. *"Antho = phool (a-n-t-h-o ~ antho)**; **"Ergo = kaam"* (ergonomics = kaam ki efficiency). Agar root yaad hai to option ghalat ho hi nahi sakta.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**"Public speaking ka dar = jeevh/tongue ka dar = Glossophobia" — root hi asli answer hota hai, '-phobia' sirf backdrop hai.**
q1008:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**was it** — "Not until the data was independently verified **was it** accepted by the journal."

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Inversion (Negative / Restrictive Adverbial ke baad Subject–Auxiliary Inversion)**

Rule simple hai: jab sentence ki shuruaat kisi **negative ya restrictive** word/phrase se hoti hai — jaise *Not until, Never, Hardly, Scarcely, Seldom, Rarely, Little, Nowhere, No sooner, Not only, Under no circumstances* — to **main clause** mein auxiliary verb subject se **pehle** aa jaata hai (jaise question mein hota hai).

Is sentence par lagao:
- "**Not until** the data was independently verified" → ye subordinate (time) clause hai; yahan **koi inversion nahi**, normal order "the data was … verified" hi rahega.
- "____ it accepted by the journal" → ye **main clause** hai, aur "it was accepted" ek **passive** hai. Negative fronting ki wajah se "it **was**" → "**was it**" ho gaya, aur "accepted" (past participle) waise hi raha.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **it was** ✘ — Inversion nahi hua. "Not until … it was accepted" galat hai; negative adverbial ke baad plain statement order allowed nahi.
- **was it** ✔ — Auxiliary "was" subject "it" se pehle aa gaya, aur passive structure "was it accepted" bilkul sahi bana.
- **did it** ✘ — "did it **accepted**" double galat: "did" ke baad **V1 (accept)** aata hai, V3 nahi; aur yahan passive chahiye tha, "did" active bana deta hai.
- **had it** ✘ — Past perfect passive hota "had it **been** accepted". "had it accepted" active ho jaata aur tense bhi galat.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail

**Structure:** Negative Adverbial + **Auxiliary + Subject** + Main Verb

Zaroori baatein:
1. Inversion sirf **main clause** mein hota hai; "not until" ke andar wala clause **normal order** mein rehta hai.
2. Jo auxiliary main clause mein already hai (is/was/has/had/do/did/will/can), wahi subject se pehle jaata hai.
3. Agar auxiliary nahi hai (active sentence), to **do/does/did** lagao — phir main verb **V1**.
4. Passive sentence mein be-verb (was/were/had been) subject se pehle aata hai.

Examples:
✔ Not until the doctor arrived **was** the patient operated upon.
✔ Not until she apologised **did** he talk to her.
✔ Never **have** I seen such a crowd.
✔ Hardly **had** I reached the station **when** the train left.
✔ No sooner **had** he left **than** it started raining.
✔ Seldom **does** he visit his village.

✘ Not until the doctor arrived the patient was operated upon.
✘ Never I have seen such a crowd.
✘ Hardly I had reached the station when the train left.
✘ No sooner he had left when it started raining. (than chahiye)

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Only then / Only when / Only after** → inversion: "Only then **did** I realise my mistake."
2. **Hardly/Scarcely … when**, **No sooner … than** — pair yaad rakho; *than* aur *when* swap karna SSC ka favourite trap hai.
3. **Conditional inversion** (if hata do): "**Had** I known, I would have helped." / "**Were** I rich…" / "**Should** you need help, call me."
4. **Not only … but also** — pehle part mein inversion: "Not only **did** he steal, but he also lied."
5. **So + adj + that** inversion: "So loud **was** the noise that we couldn't sleep."
6. **Place adverb fronting**: "Here **comes** the bus", "There **goes** the train" — par subject pronoun ho to inversion nahi: "Here **he comes**."
7. **Negative words jahan inversion NAHI hota** — "not until" ke andar wale clause mein normal order check karne wale trap questions.
8. **Under no circumstances / In no way / At no time / Nowhere / Little** → inversion: "Under no circumstances **should** you open this door."
9. Trap: **did + V3** (galat) vs **did + V1** (sahi), aur active vs passive ka confusion.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
"**Negative aage, helper aage.**" Jaise hi sentence *Not until / Never / Hardly / Seldom / No sooner* se shuru ho, samajh lo wahan **Helper + Subject + Verb** order banega — jaise question banate ho.
Aur ek line yaad rakho: *"Not until" ke andar ka hissa normal, "Not until" ke baad wala hissa inverted.*

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
Negative adverbial ("Not until…") se start hone par main clause inverted hota hai — isliye passive "it was accepted" ka roop "**was it accepted**" banega.
q1009:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Option 2** — error part (2) "until the investigation **would be** completed" mein hai; yahan **was completed** hoga.

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Time Clause Rule (Adverb Clause of Time mein 'will/would' nahi aata).**

Hinglish mein simple baat: jab sentence mein **when, while, before, after, until/till, as soon as, by the time, once, the moment, whenever** jaise time-words aate hain, to unke baad wale clause mein **will / would / shall** kabhi nahi lagate — chahe matlab future ka hi ho. Us jagah **simple present** (future ke liye) ya **simple past** (past ke liye) lagta hai.

Is sentence par apply karo:
- Main clause: "The spokesperson **refused** to comment" — ye past hai.
- Time clause: "**until** the investigation ____ completed" — 'until' ek time-word hai, isliye yahan `would` galat hai; past ki baat hai to **was** aayega: "until the investigation **was completed**".
- Yahi galti part (2) mein hai — isliye answer = **2**.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **(1) The spokesperson refused to comment** — ✔ sahi. Past tense "refused" + "to comment" (infinitive) bilkul theek; subject "spokesperson" singular, verb "refused" singular — agreement bhi sahi.
- **(2) until the investigation would be completed** — ✘ **GALAT**. Time clause ('until') mein `would` nahi aata; sahi roop: "until the investigation **was completed**".
- **(3) to avoid jeopardising** — ✔ sahi. "avoid" ke baad hamesha **gerund (V-ing)** aata hai — "avoid jeopardising". (Yahan 'avoid + to + V1' lagana galti hoti, par diya hua theek hai.)
- **(4) ongoing proceedings** — ✔ sahi. "proceedings" = legal karyavahi; adjective "ongoing" theek, koi article/preposition error nahi.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail

**Kabhi mat lagao:** when, while, before, after, until/till, as soon as, by the time, the moment, once, whenever, as long as, no sooner…than, hardly…when — inke baad **will/would/shan't** nahi.

**Kya lagao:**
- Future ka matlab → **simple present**: *I will wait until he **comes**.*
- Past ka matlab → **simple past**: *I waited until he **came**.*
- Perfect zaroori ho to → present perfect / past perfect: *We will start after he **has arrived**.*

**Exceptions (yahan 'will/would' allowed hai):**
1. **Noun clause** (jaanbujh kar sawaal/interrogative): *I don't know **when** he **will** come.* — yahan 'when' time-clause nahi, noun-clause hai.
2. **Direct question**: ***When will** you finish?*
3. **'when' = and then** (narration): *I was reading **when** the phone **rang**.* (yahan 'will' ka sawaal hi nahi)
4. **Conditional 'if' clause** mein bhi yahi logic chalta hai: *If it **rains**, we will cancel.* ('if' + present, 'will' main clause mein)

**Examples (✔ sahi vs ✘ galat):**
- ✘ I will call you as soon as I **will reach** home. → ✔ …as soon as I **reach** home.
- ✘ She stayed there until the bus **would arrive**. → ✔ …until the bus **arrived**.
- ✘ We will leave before he **will come**. → ✔ …before he **comes**.
- ✘ He will not start the work till the money **would** be sanctioned. → ✔ …till the money **is** sanctioned.
- ✔ I don't know when he **will** return. (noun clause — allowed)
- ✔ Hardly **had** he entered the class **when** the bell rang. (time clause, 'when' ke baad 'will' nahi)

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Time clause + will/would trap** — *He will inform you when the result **will be** declared* ✘ → **is** declared ✔
2. **unless + not** — ‘unless’ khud negative hai: *Unless you **don't** work hard, you will fail* ✘ → *Unless you **work hard**…* ✔
3. **If-clause structure** — *If he **will come**, I shall meet him* ✘ → *If he **comes**…* ✔
4. **no sooner…than / hardly…when** ka pair — ‘no sooner’ ke saath **than** (not ‘then’/‘that’); *No sooner **did** he arrive **than** the meeting began.*
5. **Inversion** — *Hardly **had** I reached **when** it started raining.* (helping verb subject se pehle)
6. **avoid / enjoy / mind / suggest / look forward to + V-ing** — *He avoided **to answer** ✘ → **answering** ✔
7. **Reported speech** — *He said he **would** come* ✔ (main clause ka future-in-past allowed, time clause mein nahi)
8. **until vs till vs up to** preposition use, aur **after + having + V3** — *After **having finished** the work, he left.* ✔

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"Time clause ki ghadi present mein chalti hai."**
Jahan **when/before/after/until/as soon as** likha ho, wahan **will/would** ko dekhkar turant alarm baja do — wo 'will' hi error hai. (Bas "I don't know when…" jaise noun-clause aur sawaal ko chhod dena.)

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**'Until/when/before/after/as soon as' jaise time-word ke baad future ya past ka matlab ho to bhi 'will/would' nahi — simple present/past lagao. Isliye part (2) galat hai, option 2 sahi.**
q1010:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Option (2)** — "until the investigation would be completed" mein error hai; sahi hoga "until the investigation **was** completed".

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Tense in Adverb Clause of Time (Time Clause mein `will/would` ka istemaal na karna)**

Simple Hinglish mein: Jab kisi clause ki shuruaat **when, while, until, till, before, after, as soon as, by the time, since** jaise time-words se hoti hai, to us clause mein future ya "would" wala idea hone par bhi **`will / would` nahi lagate**. Wahan:
- Future ka matlab ho → **simple present** (`comes`, `is`, `finishes`)
- Past ka matlab ho → **simple past** (`came`, `was`, `finished`)

Is sentence mein dekho:
- Main clause: "The spokesperson **refused** to comment" → past tense.
- Time clause: "until the investigation **would be completed**" → yahi galat hai. `refused` (past) ke saath time clause **simple past** mein aayega → "until the investigation **was completed**".

✔ Correct sentence: *The spokesperson refused to comment until the investigation **was completed** to avoid jeopardising ongoing proceedings.*

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **(1) "The spokesperson refused to comment"** — Sahi. Main clause simple past mein hai, structure theek hai.
- **(2) "until the investigation would be completed"** — ❌ **Yahi error hai.** Time clause (`until`) mein `would` galat hai; `was completed` chahiye.
- **(3) "to avoid jeopardising"** — Sahi. `avoid` ke baad **gerund (V-ing)** aata hai: *avoid + doing*. Purpose batane ke liye "to + verb" bhi theek hai.
- **(4) "ongoing proceedings"** — Sahi. `ongoing` (adjective) + `proceedings` (noun) ka collocation sahi hai.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail

**Kab `will/would` nahi lagega — Time Clause:**
`when, whenever, while, until, till, before, after, as soon as, by the time, once, the moment, immediately after`

| ✔ Sahi | ✘ Galat |
|---|---|
| I will wait **until he comes**. | I will wait until he **will come**. |
| She left **before the meeting started**. | She left before the meeting **would start**. |
| **As soon as he arrives**, we will begin. | As soon as he **will arrive**, we will begin. |
| **By the time you reach**, I will have finished. | By the time you **will reach**, I will have finished. |
| Wait here **till I return**. | Wait here till I **will return**. |

**Zaroori Exceptions / Traps:**

1. **Noun Clause mein `will/would` bilkul allowed hai.** Ye time clause nahi, object clause hai:
   - ✔ I don't know **when he will come**. (yahan `when` ka matlab "kis waqt" — noun clause)
   - ✔ I asked **when the train would arrive**. (Yahi trick is question jaisa lagta hai, par yahan `until` adverbial time clause hai, isliye `would` galat.)
2. **Past habit wale `would`** time clause mein aa sakta hai:
   - ✔ When he was young, he **would** swim every morning.
3. **If/Unless clause (Condition)** mein bhi `will/would` nahi:
   - ✘ If it **will rain**, we will cancel. → ✔ If it **rains**, we will cancel.
4. **`until` vs `unless`:** `until` = time tak; `unless` = agar nahi. "Until" ke saath `not` ka jodka bahut common hai: *He did not sleep until the work was done.*
5. **Sequence mat badlo:** Main clause past → time clause simple past. Main clause future → time clause simple present.

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Time clause + will/would (sabse favourite trap)** — *I shall wait here until you **return**.* (not "will return")
2. **Noun clause vs Time clause ka farq** — *I don't know when he **will** come* (✔) vs *I will leave when he **comes*** (✔, not "will come").
3. **If/Unless clause mein will** — *Unless you **work** hard, you will fail.* (not "will work")
4. **`avoid / deny / enjoy / mind / suggest` + gerund** — *He avoided **answering** the question.* (not "to answer")
5. **`Unless...not` double negative** — ✘ *Unless you don't hurry, you'll be late.* → ✔ *Unless you hurry, you'll be late.*
6. **`No sooner ... than`, `Hardly ... when`, `Scarcely ... when`** — *No sooner had he left **than** it rained.* (not "then/when")
7. **`Since` + point of time + present perfect** — *I **have lived** here since 2010.* (not "I am living since")
8. **Reported speech ka tense shift** — *He said that he **would** come.* (yahan `would` bilkul sahi — kyunki ye noun clause hai, time clause nahi.)

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"Time word + will/would = jaal."**
Jaise hi `when / until / till / before / after / as soon as / by the time` dikhe, dimaag mein alarm bajao — wahan **present ya past simple** hi lagta hai, `will/would` ko entry nahi.

Chhota mantra: **"Jab tak, jab, se pehle, ke baad — wahan `will` bhool jao, simple tense yaad."**

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
Adverb clause of time (`until`, `when`, `before`, `after`, `as soon as`) mein `will/would` kabhi nahi — past main clause ke saath **simple past** ("until the investigation **was completed**") lagta hai, isliye error part **(2)** mein hai.
q1011:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Part (1)** — "Were he to have responded promptly" is part mein error hai. (Sahi roop: **"Had he responded promptly"**)

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Conditional Sentences ki Inversion + Subjunctive Mood (unreal past condition).**

Simple Hinglish mein: Conditional sentence ke teen types hote hain, aur "if" hatakar hum subject-verb **invert** karte hain — par har type ka apna fixed inverted form hai. Inhe mix karna galat hai:

| Type | Normal (with *if*) | Inverted form |
|---|---|---|
| Future unlikely | If he should come… | **Should** he come… |
| Present/Future unreal | If he were to come… | **Were** he to come… |
| Past unreal | If he had come… | **Had** he come… |

Is sentence mein main clause hai — *"the crisis **could have been** averted"* — ye ek **past unreal result** hai (jo hua hi nahi). Aise main clause ke saath if-clause bhi **past unreal** hona chahiye, yaani **"Had he responded promptly"**.

Lekin likha hai *"**Were** he **to have responded**"* — ye **Type-2 ka "Were to"** (present/future unreal) ko **Type-3 ke perfect infinitive "have responded"** ke saath mila diya. Do types ka hybrid — isliye galat.

Sentence par ishara:
- *"Were he to have responded promptly"* → ❌ galat structure (past unreal ke liye "Had" chahiye)
- *"the crisis could have been averted"* → ✔ ye past unreal result maang raha hai "Had + S + $V_3$" wala if-clause.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **(1) "Were he to have responded promptly"** → ❌ **Error.** Past unreal condition ka inverted form "Had + subject + $V_3$" hota hai, yaani **"Had he responded promptly"**.
- **(2) "the crisis could have been"** → ✔ Passive with modal perfect ($\text{could have been} + V_3$) — bilkul theek; "been" ko part (3) ka "averted" complete karta hai.
- **(3) "averted far earlier than it ultimately was"** → ✔ Comparison theek hai. Ellipsis se "than it ultimately **was** [averted]" — verb repeat karne ki zaroorat nahi. "far earlier" (intensifier + comparative) bhi sahi.
- **(4) "saving valuable diplomatic capital"** → ✔ Present participle phrase jo poore pichle clause ka **result** batata hai (kis cheez ka fayda hua). Ye adverbial participle hai — grammatically fine.

**Note (imaandaari se):** kuch advanced / literary English mein "were to have + $V_3$" dikh jaata hai, par **SSC ki textbook grammar aur exam answer-key** ise galat maanti hai — exam mein "Had he responded" hi expected hai. Isliye exam ke liye answer **1**.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**Inversion ka matlab:** jab "if" hata dete hain, to helping verb subject se pehle aa jaati hai. Sirf teen helping verbs invert hoti hain: **had, were, should**.

**Teen conditional types (inversion ke saath):**

1. **First/Real (possible):** *If he comes → **Should** he come, I will meet him.*
2. **Second/Unreal present-future:** *If he came / were to come → **Were** he to come, I would meet him.*
   - "$Were + S + to + V_1$" — yahan **V1** hi aayega, perfect infinitive nahi.
3. **Third/Unreal past:** *If he had come → **Had** he come, I would have met him.*
   - "Had + S + $V_3$", main clause mein "would/could/might **have** + $V_3$".

**Golden pairing rule:** Main clause jis type ka, if-clause bhi usi type ka (warna "mixed conditional" ban jaata hai, jo specific situations ke liye alag structure maangta hai).

**Examples:**
- ✔ **Had** I known the truth, I would have told you.
- ✘ *Were I to have known the truth, I would have told you.* (exam mein galat)
- ✔ **Were** I to know the truth, I would tell you. (present unreal — sahi)
- ✔ **Should** you need help, call me.
- ✔ **Were** he here, he would explain everything.
- ✔ **Had** she applied on time, she could have got the job.
- ✘ *Should he had applied on time…* (types mix — galat)

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Had-inversion (3rd conditional):** *Had he studied, he would have passed.* — sabse zyada poocha jaata hai.
2. **Were-inversion (2nd conditional):** *Were I rich, I would buy a house.*
3. **Should-inversion (1st conditional):** *Should it rain, the match will be cancelled.*
4. **"If I were you"** — "were" hi aayega, ❌ *If I was you*.
5. **"wish / as if / as though" + were / had $V_3$:** *I wish I were taller.* / *He talks as if he were a king.*
6. **"It is high time / It is time" + past subjunctive:** *It is high time we **left**.* (❌ *we leave*)
7. **"would rather / would sooner" + past subjunctive:** *I would rather you **came** tomorrow.*
8. **"If only" + had $V_3$:** *If only I **had listened** to him!*
9. **Trap — "would have" if-clause mein galat:** ❌ *If I would have known…* — if-clause mein "would" nahi aata.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"JAHAAN PAST, WAHAN HAD"** —
Main clause mein *could/would/might **have** + $V_3$* dikhe → if-clause **"Had + S + $V_3$"** hi hoga.
Aur yaad rakho: **"Were to" ke baad sirf V1** ("Were he to **respond**"), **"have + $V_3$" nahi**. Bas itna pakad lo, "Were to have" jaisa hybrid kabhi galat lagega.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**Past unreal condition ka inverted form sirf "Had + subject + $V_3$" hota hai — "Were he to have + $V_3$" galat hai, isliye error Part (1) mein → answer: 1.**
q1012:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**Last option (D) — "Authorities believed the accused had been hiding in the hills."**
*(OCR mein option letters sab "C)" ho gaye hain — letters par na jao, text par jao. Sahi text yahi aakhri wala hai.)*

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Voice Change — Passive se Active (implied agent ko exposed karna + perfect-continuous infinitive ko finite clause mein kholna).**

Simple Hinglish mein: Passive sentence mein "kaam karne wala" (doer/agent) aksar chhup jaata hai. Active banate waqt us chhupe hue doer ko **subject** bana dena hota hai, aur passive ke saath jo infinitive jura hota hai usko wapas ek **poora clause** bana dena hota hai — bina tense/aspect badle.

Is sentence par lagao:

- Subject (receiver): **"The accused"** — jo believe kiya gaya.
- Passive verb: **"was believed"** (past simple passive of *believe*).
- Uske baad: **"to have been hiding"** — ye ek **perfect continuous infinitive** hai = kaam (hiding) believing se *pehle se chal raha tha aur jaari tha*.
- Doer passive mein gayab hai — context (accused, hills, capture) se doer = **"Authorities"**.
- Ab "to have been hiding" ko kholo → **"had been hiding"** (past perfect continuous), aur *that* laga do.

➡️ **The accused was believed to have been hiding…** = **Authorities believed the accused had been hiding…** ✅

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
1. **"The accused believed he was hiding in the hills."** — ✘ Meaning ulti ho gayi: ab *accused* khud believer ban gaya. Aur "was hiding" (past continuous) ne "to have been hiding" (perfect continuous) ka aspect gira diya.
2. **"Someone believed the accused had hidden in the hills."** — ✘ Agent theek hai, par **"had hidden"** = past perfect **simple** — continuous *-ing* aspect khatam; "before being captured" ka bhi pata nahi. Faithful conversion nahi.
3. **"It was believed that the accused had been hiding in the hills."** — ✘ Ye phir bhi **passive** hai (*"It was believed"*). Question active maangta hai. Direction hi galat.
4. **"Authorities believed the accused had been hiding in the hills."** — ✔ Doer = "Authorities" subject ban gaya, main verb active = "believed", aur hiding = "had been hiding" (past perfect continuous) — pura aspect waise ka waisa.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail

**Passive (agent-free) ke teen dhaanche aur unke active roop:**

| Passive structure | Ka matlab | Active mein |
|---|---|---|
| `be + V3 + to have been + V-ing` | past perfect continuous | `… had been + V-ing` |
| `be + V3 + to have + V3` | past perfect | `… had + V3` |
| `be + V3 + to be + V-ing` | past continuous | `… was/were + V-ing` |
| `be + V3 + to be + V3` | passive infinitive | `… is/was + V3` |

**Doosra hissa — agent ka khel:** Passive jab agent batata hi nahi, to active mein hum **someone / people / they / authorities / police** jaisa suitable doer daal dete hain — par **meaning ke hisaab se hi** (is sentence mein "hills + captured" → *Authorities* sabse fit).

**Yahi kaam reporting sentences mein:** *"He is said to be…"*, *"It is believed that…"* → active mein *"People say/believe that…"*.

**Examples (✔ sahi / ✘ galat):**

- ✔ Passive: *He is said to be honest.* → Active: *People say that he is honest.*
- ✔ Passive: *The thief was believed to have escaped.* → Active: *Police believed that the thief had escaped.*
- ✔ Passive: *She was known to have been helping the poor.* → Active: *People knew that she had been helping the poor.*
- ✔ Passive: *The boy is thought to be sleeping.* → Active: *People think that the boy is sleeping.*
- ✘ *Police believed the thief has escaped.* (tense mismatch — believing past, escaping usse pehle → **had escaped**)
- ✘ *Authorities believed the accused was hiding in the hills.* (perfect continuous ka bhaav gaya)

**Ahem exception:** Voice badalne se **tense aur meaning kabhi nahi badalna chahiye** — sirf *structure* badalta hai. Agar active option tense/aspect badal de, wo galat hai (jaise option 2 aur 1).

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Perfect continuous infinitive → past perfect continuous:** *"to have been doing"* hamesha *"had been doing"* banega. — *He was reported to have been smoking.*
2. **Simple perfect infinitive → past perfect:** *"to have + V3"* → *"had + V3"*. — *She was known to have won.*
3. **"It is said/believed/reported/thought that…"** passive → active: *People say/believe/report that…*
4. **Agent-less passive mein doer supply karna:** *someone, people, they, authorities* — meaning se decide karo.
5. **Double passive trap:** *"being captured"* jaise passive gerund ko kabhi-kabhi active mein *"before he was captured"* karna padta hai.
6. **Reporting verbs ka personal passive:** *He is considered to be a genius* → *People consider him a genius.*
7. **Tense shift dhundo, change mat karo:** Student *"was"* ko *"is"* ya *"has"* kar deta hai — yahi sabse bada trap.
8. **Continuous vs simple ka farq:** *"to have been + V-ing"* aur *"to have + V3"* ko options mein mix kar dete hain — *-ing* gaya to answer gaya.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"Chhupa doer bahar laao; `to have been` pe `had been`, `to have` pe `had`, `to be` pe `was/were`."**
Matlab: passive ke *infinitive code* ko padho aur seedha past-clause mein convert karo — tense same rakho, `-ing` mat chhodo.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
Passive→Active = **agent ko subject banao + `to have been hiding` ko `had been hiding` khol do** — "had hidden" nahi, warna aspect mar jaata hai.

**Sahi option (D): Authorities believed the accused had been hiding in the hills.**
q1013:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**D — "comprises of"** (yahi galat part hai)

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Preposition + Verb (Correct usage of "comprise")** — yani verb ke saath kaunsa preposition lagega, aur **kab koi preposition lagega hi nahi**.

Rule simple hai: **"comprise" ek transitive verb hai** — matlab iske baad seedha object aata hai, koi preposition nahi.

- **"comprise"** = consist of / include / be made up of. Ye apne aap mein "of" ka matlab le chuka hai.
- Isliye "comprises **of**" likhna galat hai — ye "consist **of**" jaisa double ho jata hai.

**Is sentence par kaise laga:** sentence hai — *"This test **comprises of** grammar, vocabulary and reading comprehension."*
Yahan subject `This test` ke baad verb `comprises` hai, aur uske aage ka wala part `grammar, vocabulary and reading comprehension` = object. To object ke pehle **"of" ki koi zaroorat nahi**. `of` hata do, "comprises" rakho — sentence sahi ho jayega: *"This test comprises grammar, vocabulary and reading comprehension."*

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **A. grammar, vocabulary** — Sahi part. Ye sirf object list hai; isme koi grammatical error nahi.
- **B. This test** — Sahi part. Subject hai; singular subject hai to `comprises` (singular verb) bhi theek baithta hai.
- **C. and reading comprehension** — Sahi part. Parallelism bhi sahi hai (grammar, vocabulary **and** reading comprehension).
- **D. comprises of** — ✘ Galat. `comprise` ke saath `of` nahi lagta. Yahan **"comprises"** hona chahiye. Isliye yahi error hai.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**"Comprise" ke 3 sahi istemaal aur 1 galat:**

| Structure | Sahi/Galat | Example |
|---|---|---|
| X comprises Y | ✔ | The committee comprises ten members. |
| X consists of Y | ✔ | The committee consists of ten members. |
| X is composed of Y | ✔ | The committee is composed of ten members. |
| X comprises of Y | ✘ | The committee comprises of ten members. |

**Logic yaad rakho:** *Whole comprises the parts; parts compose the whole.*

- ✔ The country **comprises** 28 states.
- ✔ The country **consists of** 28 states.
- ✔ The country **is composed of** 28 states.
- ✘ The country **comprises of** 28 states.
- ✘ The country **is comprised of** 28 states. (Traditional/SSC grammar mein ye bhi galat mana jata hai — passive mein "comprise" use na karo; "is composed of" likho.)

**4-6 example sentences (✔ vs ✘):**
- ✔ The syllabus **comprises** five units.
- ✘ The syllabus **comprises of** five units.
- ✔ The team **comprises** eleven players.
- ✘ The team **is comprised of** eleven players. (SSC ke rule ke hisaab se galat)
- ✔ The book **consists of** ten chapters.
- ✘ The book **consists** ten chapters. (ulta error — yahan `of` chahiye)

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
Ye "verb + extra preposition" ka family hai — SSC ka evergreen trap. 6-8 rules:

1. **discuss** → object seedha aata hai, `about` nahi.
   ✔ We discussed the plan. ✘ We discussed **about** the plan.
2. **emphasize** → `on` nahi.
   ✔ He emphasized the need for practice. ✘ He emphasized **on** the need.
3. **await** → `for` nahi.
   ✔ I await your reply. ✘ I await **for** your reply.
4. **reach** → `at/to` nahi.
   ✔ We reached Delhi. ✘ We reached **at** Delhi.
5. **order / request** → object ke baad `for` nahi.
   ✔ She ordered a coffee. ✘ She ordered **for** a coffee.
6. **comprise / consist / compose** → teeno ka structure alag, milao mat (upar table).
7. **invest in** → yahan `in` ZAROORI hai.
   ✔ He invested in mutual funds. ✘ He invested mutual funds.
8. **listen to / reply to / respond to** → `to` zaroori.
   ✔ Please reply to my email. ✘ Please reply my email.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"Comprise" ke andar hi "of" chhupa hai.**
Yaad rakho chart: **Comprise = no 'of' | Consist = 'of' | Composed = 'of'**

Ek line ka mantra: *"Comprise khud poora hai, usko `of` ki zaroorat nahi."*

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**"Comprise" ke baad kabhi "of" mat lagao — sirf "comprises + object" ya "consists of / is composed of" likho, isliye is question mein error "comprises of" (option D) hai.**
q1014:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**D — "accuses him for"** (yani is segment mein error hai; sahi roop hoga — *accuses him **of*** a lack of morality).

> Note: option ka letter book/app ke layout par depend karta hai. Pehchan **content** se karo — jo option "accuses him **for**" dikhaye, wahi answer hai. Diye gaye order mein wahi option **D** hai (A = She often, B = a lack of morality, C = No error, D = accuses him for).

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Appropriate Preposition (Verb + Preposition collocation).**

English mein kuch verbs ke saath ek fixed (pakka) preposition hi aata hai — badalna allowed nahi. Yahan verb **accuse** hai, aur *accuse* ke baad hamesha **of** aata hai, kabhi **for** nahi:

$$\text{accuse} + \text{someone} + \boxed{\text{of}} + \text{something}$$

Is sentence par apply karo:
- "She often **accuses him**" → yahan tak theek hai.
- "**for** a lack of morality" → ye galat preposition hai. Yahan chahiye **of** → "*accuses him **of** a lack of morality*".

Trap kya hai: **blame** ke saath *for* aata hai — *blame him **for** a lack of morality* ✔. Student "blame for" yaad rakhta hai aur usi flow mein "accuse for" bol deta hai. Isliye ye question 90% students galat karte hain.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **A. She often** — ✔ Sahi. Subject "She" + adverb "often", koi grammatical error nahi. (Sentence mein "She, often," ke extra commas hain, par SSC error-spotting mein punctuation ko error nahi maana jaata.)
- **B. a lack of morality** — ✔ Sahi. "a lack of + noun" ek standard phrase hai (*lack of confidence, lack of money*). Yahan *morality* abstract noun hai — bilkul valid.
- **C. No error** — ✘ Galat option. Sentence mein error hai (preposition), isliye "No error" kabhi answer nahi ho sakta.
- **D. accuses him for** — ✘ **Yahi error hai.** "accuse" ke saath preposition **of** aata hai, **for** nahi. Sahi: *accuses him **of** a lack of morality*.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
Verb + Preposition ka rule: verb ka meaning jaisa fixed hai, uska preposition bhi fixed hai. Isliye inhe **"jodi"** yaad karo, akela verb nahi.

**Sabse zyada poochhe jaane wale pairs:**

| Verb | Preposition | Matlab / Example |
|---|---|---|
| accuse | **of** | *He was accused **of** theft.* |
| blame | **for** | *They blamed him **for** the failure.* |
| charge | **with** | *He was charged **with** murder.* |
| convict | **of** | *The court convicted him **of** fraud.* |
| suspect | **of** | *Police suspect him **of** lying.* |
| congratulate | **on** | *I congratulated her **on** her success.* |
| praise | **for** | *The teacher praised him **for** his honesty.* |

✔ *She accused him **of** a lack of morality.*
✘ *She accused him **for** a lack of morality.*

✔ *The manager blamed the clerk **for** the delay.*
✘ *The manager blamed the clerk **of** the delay.*

✔ *He was charged **with** corruption.*
✔ *They convicted her **of** cheating.*
✔ *Everyone praised him **for** his bravery.*
✔ *Are you accusing me **of** lying?*

**Exception / dhyan ki baat:** Har preposition "meaning" se nahi aata, collocation se aata hai — isliye logic lagane se galat hoga. Yaad rakhna hi padega. Aur ek verb ke saath do preposition tabhi aate hain jab verb ka meaning/roop badle (jaise *agree **with** a person* vs *agree **to** a proposal*) — yahan aisa kuch nahi, *accuse* ke saath sirf **of**.

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **accuse of / blame for / charge with** — sabse common trap. *"The police charged him for theft"* ✘ → **with** ✔.
2. **"discuss about" trap** — *We discussed about the plan* ✘ → *We **discussed** the plan* ✔ (koi preposition nahi).
3. **"Since vs For"** — *since* + point of time (*since 2010*), *for* + period (*for three years*). *"I have been here since three hours"* ✘.
4. **"reach at / order" trap** — *reach* ke baad preposition nahi (*We reached the station* ✔), *order* bhi transitive (*He ordered a coffee* ✔, *ordered for* ✘).
5. **"married with"** ✘ → *married **to*** ✔.
6. **"comprise of"** ✘ → *comprise* akela ya *consist **of*** ✔.
7. **"superior than"** ✘ → *superior **to*** ✔ (senior, junior, inferior — sab **to**).
8. **"listen/reply/approach"** — verb ke baad *to* zaroori: *listen **to** me*, *reply **to** the letter*, *approach **to** the problem* (noun) vs *approach the teacher* (verb, no prep).
9. **angry with / angry at** — vyakti par **with** (*angry with him*), cheez/vyavhaar par **at** (*angry at his behaviour*).
10. **die of / from / in** — bimari se *die **of***, injury se *die **from***, accident mein *die **in***.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"OF = Offence"** — jab kisi par **ilzaam (offence)** lagta hai, tab **accuse + of**.
**"FOR = Fault dene ke liye"** — jab sirf **dosh (fault)** dete hain, tab **blame + for**.
**"WITH = Warrant/Warrant-style charge"** — court/police ka formal charge → **charge + with**.

Ek line mein: **Accuse → Of, Blame → For, Charge → With.** Teen alag verbs, teen pakke saathi.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
*Accuse* ke saath hamesha **of** — "accuses him **for**" galat hai, sahi hai **"accuses him of a lack of morality"** → answer option D.
q1015:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**C — To my point of view** (isse "From my point of view" ya "In my opinion" banana chahiye).

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Fixed Preposition + Idiom (Prepositional Phrase)** — kuch phrases mein preposition fix hota hai; use badalna allowed nahi.

Sentence ko dekho: *"**To** my point of view he should not have behaved in such a manner."*

- "point of view" ke saath hamesha **from** aata hai → **from my point of view**.
- Ya phir "opinion" ke saath **in** aata hai → **in my opinion**.
- **"To my point of view"** — ye combination English mein exist nahi karta. Isliye error option **C** mein hai.

Baaki parts bilkul sahi hain:
- "he **should not have behaved**" → past ka criticism/modal perfect, structure sahi.
- "**behaved**" → verb ka past participle, sahi.
- "**in such a manner**" → "manner" ke saath "in" sahi hai (in a manner / in such a manner).

**Corrected sentence:** *From my point of view, he should not have behaved in such a manner.* (ya *In my opinion, he should not have behaved in such a manner.*)

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **A. should not have** — ✔ Sahi. "should not have + V3" ka sahi pattern hai (past ke baare mein regret/criticism).
- **B. behaved** — ✔ Sahi. "have" ke baad hamesha V3 (past participle) aata hai, aur "behaved" V3 hai.
- **C. To my point of view** — ✘ **GALAT yahi hai.** "To" ki jagah "From" chahiye ("from my point of view") ya poora phrase badal kar "In my opinion" karo.
- **D. in such a manner** — ✔ Sahi. "manner" ke pehle "in" ka prayog standard hai.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**Concept:** Preposition kabhi meaning se decide nahi hota, balki **collocation (fixed pairing)** se decide hota hai. Noun/adjective/verb ke saath kaunsa preposition lagega, ye yaad rakhna padta hai.

"Point of view" ek fixed phrase hai — iske pehle sirf **from** aata hai:
- ✔ **From** my point of view, the plan is risky.
- ✔ **From** a teacher's point of view, this is unfair.

"Opinion" ke saath **in** aata hai:
- ✔ **In** my opinion, he is right.
- ✘ To my opinion, he is right.

"Mind" ke saath **to** aata hai:
- ✔ **To** my mind, he is right.

Isliye sentence mein "to" galat hai — kyunki yahan phrase "point of view" hai, "mind" nahi.

**Aur examples (✔ vs ✘):**
- ✔ *From my point of view, this movie is boring.* / ✘ *To my point of view, this movie is boring.*
- ✔ *In my opinion, he should apologise.* / ✘ *According to me, he should apologise.*
- ✔ *To my mind, this is the best solution.* / ✘ *To my point of view, this is the best solution.*
- ✔ *She behaved in a rude manner.* / ✘ *She behaved on a rude manner.*
- ✔ *The teacher was angry **with** the boy **at** his behaviour.* (person → with, thing → at)
- ✔ *He is good **at** maths.* / ✘ *He is good **in** maths.*

**Exceptions / dhyan ki baat:** Roz-marra ki bolchaal mein log "in my point of view" bol dete hain, par **standard written English aur SSC** mein sirf **from my point of view** ya **in my opinion** chalta hai. Exam mein colloquial usage nahi chalta.

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **"According to me"** galat → *In my opinion* / *According to my teacher* (third person ke saath "according to" chalta hai). ✘ *According to me, this is wrong.*
2. **Discuss about** galat → *discuss* (no preposition). ✘ *Let's discuss about the issue.*
3. **Reach at/to** → *reach* akela. ✘ *I reached at Delhi.* ✔ *I reached Delhi.*
4. **Married with** → *married to*. ✘ *She is married with Rahul.* ✔ *married to Rahul.*
5. **Superior than** → *superior to* (Latin comparative words: senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, preferable). ✔ *This is superior to that.*
6. **Comprise of** → *comprise* (ya *comprise* = consist of). ✘ *The team comprises of 11 players.* ✔ *comprises 11 players.*
7. **Prefer ... than** → *prefer ... to*. ✘ *I prefer tea than coffee.* ✔ *I prefer tea to coffee.*
8. **Different than** → *different from*. ✔ *His answer is different from mine.*
9. **Averse to / addicted to / confide in / deprived of** — in sab fixed pairs ko yaad rakho.
10. **Trap:** Error-spotting mein SSC kabhi preposition nahi, kabhi "should have + V3" ya "modal" par trap lagata hai — isliye pehle dekho kaunsa part **phrase-level fixed pairing** tod raha hai.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"Point of view" ke aage sirf "FROM" — jaise aankh se dekhne ke liye "from" aata hai. Aur "opinion" ke aage sirf "IN".**
Chhota formula: **FROM + point of view | IN + my opinion | TO + my mind** — teen alag phrases, teen alag prepositions, mix mat karo.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
"To my point of view" galat hai — **from my point of view** ya **in my opinion** likho; fixed prepositions ko idiom ki tarah ratto.
q1016:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**B — "is invisible from"** — error isi segment mein hai; sahi preposition **"to"** hoga: "*...that is invisible **to** the naked eye*".

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Fixed Preposition (Adjective + Preposition Collocation).**

Kuch adjectives ke saath preposition **fix** hota hai, hum apni marzi se badal nahi sakte. **"invisible" ke baad jab *perceiver* (jo cheez dekh raha hai) aata hai, to "to" lagta hai** — *invisible to the eye / to the naked eye / to humans*.

Sentence mein dekho: "*There is a whole world out there that is invisible **from** the naked eye.*" — yahan "the naked eye" **perceiver** hai (wo aankh jo dekh rahi hai), koi jagah nahi. Isliye **"invisible from"** galat hai → **"invisible to"** hona chahiye.

Note (confusion door karo): **"invisible from"** bhi galat nahi hai — par tabhi, jab baat **vantage point / jagah** ki ho: *"The moon is invisible **from** this city."* Yahan "from" ke baad **place** hai, person/eye nahi.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **A — "the naked eye"** : ✔ Sahi. "naked eye" ek idiom hai = bina kisi instrument ke aankh (binoculor/microscope ke bina). Preposition ka error isme nahi hai.
- **B — "is invisible from"** : ✘ **Yahi error hai.** "invisible **to** the naked eye" hona chahiye. ("from" sirf jagah ke liye.)
- **C — "There is a whole world"** : ✔ Sahi. "There is" existential structure, subject "a whole world" singular → "is" bilkul theek.
- **D — "out there that"** : ✔ Sahi. "out there" adverbial phrase + "that" restrictive relative pronoun (antecedent = "a whole world") — dono grammatically fine.

**Corrected sentence:** *There is a whole world out there that is invisible **to** the naked eye.*

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**Part 1 — "to" wale adjectives (perceiver/relation)** :
visible **to**, invisible **to**, audible **to**, accessible **to**, agreeable **to**, acceptable **to**, similar **to**, equal **to**, preferable **to**, superior **to**, inferior **to**, senior **to**, junior **to**, prior **to**, loyal **to**, faithful **to**, harmful **to**, beneficial **to**, addicted **to**, accustomed **to**, averse **to**, prone **to**, liable **to**, immune **to**, susceptible **to**, known **to**, married **to**, engaged **to**, devoted **to**.

**Part 2 — "to" vs "from" ka logic** :
- **to** = *kiski nazar/kiski sunne ki shakti ko* (perceiver) → The bacteria are invisible **to** the naked eye.
- **from** = *kis jagah se dekhne par* (viewpoint) → The stage is invisible **from** the back rows.

**Part 3 — Exceptions / badalne wale cases** :
- **known to** (person) par **known for** (quality): He is known **to** me / He is known **for** his honesty.
- **angry with** (person) par **angry at** (behaviour/thing): She is angry **with** me / **at** my behaviour.
- **good at**, **weak in**, **proficient in**, **confident of/about**.

**Examples:**
- ✔ The stars are invisible **to** the naked eye.
- ✘ The stars are invisible **from** the naked eye.
- ✔ The whistle is audible **to** dogs.
- ✔ The music was audible **from** the street. (jagah hai, isliye "from" ✔)
- ✔ This cloth is superior **to** that one. (✘ superior than)
- ✔ He is senior **to** me. (✘ senior than)

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Preferable to** — ✘ Coffee is preferable **than** tea. ✔ Coffee is preferable **to** tea.
2. **Superior/Inferior to** — ✘ This is superior **than** that. ✔ **to**.
3. **Senior/Junior to** — ✘ He is senior **than** me. ✔ **to**.
4. **Similar to** — ✘ similar **with** my idea. ✔ similar **to**.
5. **Discuss / Comprise / Reach** — ye transitive hain, inke baad preposition nahi: ✘ discuss **about** the matter, ✘ comprise **of** five members, ✘ reach **at** the station.
6. **Suffer from (disease) vs suffer for (mistake)** — He suffers **from** malaria / You will suffer **for** your carelessness. **Die of (disease), die from (injury/cause), die in (accident)**.
7. **Listen to / reply to / wait for / apologise to** — ✘ listen me / wait him. ✔ **listen to** me / **wait for** him.
8. **Provided with vs provided by** — We are provided **with** books / books are provided **by** the school.
9. **Visible/Audible/Accessible + to** — SSC ka favourite: "*These rays are not visible ____ the human eye*" → **to**.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"To kisne dekha? — Aankh ne dekha!"** — jab jawab ho *kiski aankh / kiski nazar / kiska kaan*, to **"to"** aayega (visible **to**, invisible **to**, audible **to**). Aur jab jawab ho *kahan se dekh rahe ho*, to **"from"** (visible **from the terrace**). Sentence mein "naked eye" = aankh (perceiver) → **to**.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**"invisible / visible / audible" ke baad perceiver (aankh, kaan, insaan) aaye to hamesha "to" — "from" sirf jagah (place) ke liye.**
q1017:
## ✅ Sahi answer
**A — "Not complying by"** — yahan `by` galat hai; **comply** ke saath hamesha **with** aata hai, isliye sahi roop hai **"Not complying with any of the laws"**.

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Fixed Preposition (Verb + Preposition Collocation).**

Kuch verbs ke saath ek hi preposition "fix" ho jaata hai — dictionary ka hissa ban jaata hai, meaning ke hisaab se badla nahi ja sakta. Aise verbs ko **prepositional verbs** kehte hain.

- **comply + with** = kisi rule/law/order/request ko maanna, paalan karna.
- **comply + by** sirf tab aata hai jab aage **time/deadline** ho — jaise *"You must comply by 5 p.m."*, *"comply by 31 March"*. Yahan "by" = "tak" (deadline).

IS sentence par lagao: *"Not **complying by** any of the laws…"* — dekho, `comply` ke baad **`any of the laws`** aa raha hai, jo ek **object** (cheez) hai, koi **time** nahi. Object ke saath "by" nahi lagta → "by" yahan galat hai. Sahi: **comply with any of the laws**.

Baaki sentence check karo (taaki confirm ho ki error sirf ek hi hai):
- "Not complying with any of the laws" = gerund phrase, ek singular subject ki tarah → uske saath **can land** (singular) ✔ sahi.
- "any of the laws" — plural noun, determiner "any of" ke saath ✔ sahi.
- "land you … trouble" — "land + object" ✔ sahi.

⚠️ Ek imaandar note: idiom ki standard form **"land someone in trouble"** hai (*"This can land you **in** serious trouble"*), "into" nahi — "into" usually movement/change of state ke liye aata hai (*walked into the room*). Kai books isliye C ko bhi nishaan-zad karti hain. Lekin `comply by` ek **pakka, bina-shak preposition error** hai, aur error-spotting mein wahi primary error hota hai — isliye **A** hi answer hai. Is point ko yaad rakho, confuse mat hona.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **A. Not complying by** → ✘ **Galat.** `comply` ke baad object (laws) ke saath **with** aata hai, "by" nahi. Yahi question ka error hai.
- **B. any of the laws** → ✔ Sahi. "any of + plural noun" bilkul valid hai; koi article/preposition problem nahi.
- **C. land you into serious trouble** → ✔ Is paper mein sahi maana gaya. (Standard idiom "land in trouble" hai, isliye "into" ideal nahi — par is question ka intended error A hai. Exam mein ek hi error hota hai, aur wahi sabse definite rule-based error chunte hain.)
- **D. can land you** → ✔ Sahi. Modal *can* + base verb *land* + object *you* — structure bilkul theek.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail

**Fixed prepositions ke 3 groups (SSC ke liye zaroori):**

| Verb | Sahi preposition | Galat (aam galti) |
|---|---|---|
| comply | **with** | comply ~~to~~ / ~~by~~ (object ke saath) |
| abide | **by** | abide ~~with~~ |
| adhere | **to** | adhere ~~with~~ |
| conform | **to** | conform ~~with~~ |
| consist | **of** | consist ~~off~~ |
| accuse | **of** | accuse ~~for~~ |
| deprived | **of** | deprived ~~from~~ |
| capable | **of** | capable ~~to~~ |
| married | **to** | married ~~with~~ |
| prefer | **to** | prefer ~~than~~ |
| superior / inferior | **to** | superior ~~than~~ |
| depend / insist | **on** | depend ~~upon~~ (chalta hai, par "on" safe) |
| listen / reply | **to** | listen ~~at~~ |

**Noun form bhi yaad rakho:** `compliance` ke saath bhi **with** — *"in compliance **with** the rules"*, *"non-compliance **with** the law"*.

**Examples (✔ sahi vs ✘ galat):**
1. ✔ All staff must **comply with** the safety rules. ✘ All staff must **comply by** the safety rules.
2. ✔ You must **comply by** 31 December. *(yahan by = deadline, sahi hai — yahi trap hai!)*
3. ✔ He refused to **abide by** the court's order. ✘ He refused to **abide with** the court's order.
4. ✔ Every member must **adhere to** the society's rules. ✘ …must **adhere with** the society's rules.
5. ✔ This mistake can **land you in** serious trouble. ✘ …can **land you into** serious trouble. *(idiom)*
6. ✔ The committee discussed the matter. ✘ The committee **discussed about** the matter. *(discuss ke saath koi preposition nahi)*

**Exception/trap:** kabhi kabhi "by" verb ke saath nahi, **time** ke saath lagta hai — *pay by Monday, comply by 6 pm, submit by Friday*. Sentence mein aage **date/time** ho to "by" sahi; aage **rule/law/order (object)** ho to "with".

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **comply with vs comply by** — jaise yahi question. Deadline ho to *by*, rule ho to *with*.
2. **abide by** — *"Citizens must abide by the law."* Kabhi "abide with" nahi (except poetic "Abide with me").
3. **adhere to / conform to / accede to** — *"Products must conform to ISI standards."*
4. **Redundant preposition** — *discuss about*, *order about*, *reach at*, *return back*, *comprise of* — sab galat. ✔ *reach the station*, ✔ *comprises five parts*.
5. **Verb jisme preposition nahi lagta** — *attack, resemble, enter, accompany, marry (someone), discuss, order, reach*.
6. **Wrong preposition replacement** — *"married with"* → **married to**; *"prefer coffee than tea"* → **prefer coffee to tea**; *"superior than"* → **superior to**; *"listen at"* → **listen to**.
7. **Idiom/collocation based error** — *land in trouble*, *get into trouble*, *be in hot water*, *take to task* — preposition fix hota hai.
8. **Omission/Insertion questions** — "comply ____ the rules" mein blank par **with** bharna hota hai.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
Ek line ka formula yaad karo:

> **"COMPLY WITH the law, ABIDE BY the rule, ADHERE TO the policy."**

Aur discrimination trick: **`BY` = Band time (deadline)**, **`WITH` = With-wala object (law/rule/order)**.
Yani: *"Comply **by** Friday (time), comply **with** the rules (cheez)."*

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
`comply` ke saath **with** (rules/laws/orders) aur **by** sirf deadline ke saath — isliye "Not complying **by** any of the laws" galat, sahi hai **"Not complying with any of the laws"** → **Option A**.

- **their criticism in heart.** — ✘ **Galat.** Idiom hai "take **to** heart" → yahan "in" ki jagah "to" chahiye. Yahi answer hai.
- **and was quite harsh** — ✔ Sahi. Linking verb "was" ke baad adjective "harsh" bilkul sahi; "not happy" ke saath parallel structure bhi ban raha hai.

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**1) "take to heart" (transitive idiom):** *take + object + to heart* — dil se lena, bura maanna.
- ✔ She took her teacher's advice **to** heart.
- ✘ She took her teacher's advice **in** heart.

**2) Ye "take heart" se alag hai!** *take heart (from something)* = himmat pakadna, hausla paana. Isme object nahi aata aur "from" lagta hai.
- ✔ The players took heart from the early goal.

**3) "in" wala roop sirf possessive ke saath:** *in one's heart / in one's heart of hearts* = andar se.
- ✔ **In my heart**, I knew he was right. (yahan "in" theek hai, kyunki possessive "my" hai aur ye koi idiom nahi, simple phrase hai)

- ✔ Learn the poem **by heart**. (✘ with heart)

- ✔ She waited **with a heavy heart**.
- ✔ He **set his heart on** that bike.
- ✔ The boss **took him to task** for the delay. (matlab: daantna — "take to heart" se bilkul alag; ye SSC ka favourite trap hai.)

**5) Fixed-preposition wale "take" phrases (ratne layak):**

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **"take to heart" vs "take heart"** — dono ka matlab alag; paper dono option rakh deta hai. Ex: *He took heart from the news.* ✔ / *He took heart his failure.* ✘
2. **"take to task"** (daantna) vs **"take to heart"** (dil se lena) — meaning-based trap.
3. **Linking verb + adjective vs adverb:** *The jury was quite **harsh**.* ✔ (✘ harshly) — "was/seem/look/feel" ke baad adjective.
4. **Collective noun agreement:** *The jury **was**/were divided.* — Indian/SSC pattern mein singular "was" chalta hai; "their" (jury ke liye) bhi acceptable.
5. **"happy with" vs "happy about/at"** — *happy with the performance* ✔ (kisi cheez se santusht), *happy about the result* bhi chalta hai; *happy on* ✘.
6. **idiom/preposition with "lose":** *lose heart* (hausla khona) vs *loose* (dheela) — spelling trap.
7. **"by heart / at heart / with a heavy heart"** — teen alag prepositions, ek hi word "heart".
8. **Preposition ke baad noun vs gerund:** *took to **criticising*** (preposition + V-ing) ✔, *took to criticise* ✘ — "to" yahan preposition hai, infinitive nahi.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
> **"Dil par lena = TO heart."**
> "To" = taraf/dil tak pahunchana — advice/criticism dil **tak** pahunch gayi.
> Aur **"in" sirf tab** jab aage possessive ho: **in my heart**, **in his heart of hearts**.
> Chhota formula: **take + cheez + TO heart** (idiom) | **in + my/his/her + heart** (simple phrase).

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**"Take (something) TO heart" hi sahi idiom hai; "in heart" galat — "in" ke saath possessive hona zaroori hai (in my heart), isliye error wala segment hai "their criticism in heart." → "to heart".**

## ✅ Sahi answer
**Option C — "spread at everything"** (isi segment mein error hai).
Correct sentence: *"Darkness spilled like ink and began to **spread over everything**."* — ya *"spread across/everywhere"*. Galti preposition **"at"** ki hai.

> Note: Tumhare option list mein letter OCR se thoda shift ho sakta hai, par culprit segment ek hi hai — **"spread at everything"**. Error option ke letter se nahi, segment ke preposition se pehchana jata hai.

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Prepositional Collocation (Verb + Preposition) — "spread" ke baad ka preposition.**

Simple Hinglish mein: **"spread"** ka matlab hai *phailna* (spread over a surface/area). Jab koi cheez *area ya surface par phailti* hai, to uske saath aata hai **over / across / through / all over / to** — kabhi **at** nahi. "At" ka kaam hai **ek exact point / nishana** dikhana (aim at, throw at, look at). Phailav (spread) ek *point* nahi, ek *area* hota hai — isliye "at" wahan bilkul fit nahi baithta.

IS sentence par lagao:
- **"Darkness spilled"** → theek (spill = behna/tapakna, intransitive yahan sahi).
- **"like ink"** → theek (simile — jaise syahi, koi grammar error nahi).
- **"and began to"** → theek ("began + to-infinitive" perfectly valid).
- **"spread at everything"** → ❌ **Yahin error hai.** Yahan "at" point/aim ka sense de raha hai, jo darkness ke phailne ke saath match nahi karta. Chahiye: **spread over / across / everywhere**.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat
- **A – "Darkness spilled"** ✔ Sahi: "spill" yahan intransitive verb hai (behna/phailna) — "Darkness spilled like ink" bilkul valid imagery hai.
- **B – "and began to"** ✔ Sahi: "began" ke baad to-infinitive ("to spread") aata hai — koi error nahi.
- **C – "spread at everything"** ✘ **Galat — yahi answer hai**: "spread" ke saath "at" nahi lagta; "over/across/through/to" lagta hai.
- **D – "like ink"** ✔ Sahi: "like" yahan preposition/simile hai (jaise), aur "spilled like ink" sahi collocation hai. (Haan, "as ink" galat hota, par "like ink" theek hai.)

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail
**Verb + Preposition collocation** ka matlab: har verb apne saath ek fixed preposition leke chalta hai. Isse badalna = error.

**"Spread" ke saath correct prepositions (area/phailav ke liye):**
- spread **over** (surface ke upar)
- spread **across** (ek chhor se doosre chhor tak)
- spread **through / throughout** (andar-aandar har jagah)
- spread **to** (ek jagah se doosri jagah tak pahunchna)

**"At" kab use hota hai:** sirf **point/nishana/rate** ke liye — *look at, aim at, throw at, point at, laugh at, at 5 o'clock, at 20 km/h*.

**Examples:**
- ✔ Ink spread **over** the paper.
- ✔ The rumour spread **across** the town.
- ✔ The fire spread **through** the building.
- ✔ The smell spread **all over** the room.
- ✔ The infection spread **to** his lungs.
- ✘ The ink spread **at** the paper. (galat — "at" point dikhata hai)
- ✘ The news spread **at** the whole city. (galat)
- ✔ Look **at** the blackboard. (yahan "at" sahi — point/nishana)
- ✔ He aimed **at** the target. (sahi — aim ka point)

**Exception/trap:** "at" kabhi-kabhi lagta hai jab rate aa jaye — *"The fire spread at an alarming speed"*. Wahan "at" **speed** ke saath juda hai (at a speed), spread ke saath nahi. Isliye "spread at an alarming speed" ✔ par "spread at everything" ✘.

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai
1. **Spread over/across** — ✘ "spread at" / "spread on". ✔ *Panic spread **over** the crowd.*
2. **"reach" ke baad koi preposition nahi** — ✘ reach **at** the station → ✔ *reach the station*.
3. **arrive at / in** (never "arrive to") — ✔ *arrive **at** the airport* (chhoti jagah), ✔ *arrive **in** Delhi* (badi jagah).
4. **"enter" ke baad koi preposition nahi** — ✘ enter **into** the room → ✔ *enter the room* ("enter into" sirf agreement/discussion ke liye).
5. **"discuss" ke baad koi preposition nahi** — ✘ *discuss **about** the matter* → ✔ *discuss the matter*.
6. **at / in / on ka base rule** — *at* = point (*at the door*), *in* = enclosed space (*in the room*), *on* = surface (*on the table*).
7. **"comprise of"** ✘ → ✔ *comprise* (no "of") / *consist of* / *composed of*.
8. **Over-generalise "at" ka trap** — students "look at, laugh at, good at" dekh kar har jagah "at" laga dete hain; par phailav wale verbs (spread, scatter, stretch, extend, flow) **over/across/through** lete hain.

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick
**"AT = tir (arrow) — nishana/point. OVER/ACROSS = phailav (chadar)."**
Jahan cheez *phail* rahi ho (darkness, ink, fire, rumour, smell) — wahan **over/across/through**. Jahan *nishana* ya *point* ho (aim, look, throw, point) — wahan **at**. Darkness kisi ek point par nahi phailti, poore area par phailti hai → **over everything**, not *at everything*.

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**"Spread" aur baaki phailav-verbs ke saath 'at' kabhi nahi — use over / across / through / to; 'at' sirf point aur nishane ke liye.**

**from colours** — is segment mein **'from'** galat hai; sahi preposition **'with'** hoga: *"…was busy splashing the wall **with** colours."*

## 📏 Kaunsa rule laga
**Rule: Preposition (Appropriate Preposition — "with" for material/means)**

Simple Hinglish: Jab kisi cheez ko **kisi padarth/maadhyam se bharo, poto, chhidko, sajavo ya dhako** — matlab jab *substance* bata rahe ho "kis cheez se kaam hua" — tab verb ke baad **WITH** aata hai, **FROM nahi**. **FROM** sirf **source/origin** (kahan se aaya) ke liye hota hai.

Is sentence par kaise laga:
- Karta (subject): **The Japanese artist Yoh Nagao** — ✔ theek (appositive/naam).
- Verb: **was busy** — ✔ theek (past tense, "was busy + V-ing" pattern).
- Kaam: **splashing the wall** — ✔ theek (busy ke baad gerund `splashing`).
- Maadhyam (kis se chhidka?): warna **from colours** ✘ → yahan bata raha hai wall ko *colours se* chhidka gaya, yaani instrument/material. Isliye **WITH colours** ✔.
  - Compare: *paint* **se** potna = *cover the wall* **with** paint. Colour koi *source* nahi, wo *material* hai — isliye "from" bilkul galat.

**Corrected sentence:** The Japanese artist Yoh Nagao was busy splashing the wall **with** colours.

## 🔍 Har option kyun sahi / galat

| Option | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| The Japanese artist | ✔ sahi | "The + adjective + noun" — sahi article aur appositive structure. |
| was busy | ✔ sahi | Past tense "was" + *busy* — singular subject (*The artist*) ke saath sahi agreement; *busy* ke baad `V-ing` ka rule bhi satisfied. |
| splashing the wall | ✔ sahi | *busy* ke baad gerund (`busy doing something`) — infinitive (*busy to splash*) galat hota. |
| **from colours** | ✘ **galat** | Material/means ke liye **with** chahiye, **from** nahi. Isi segment mein error hai — yahi answer. |

## 📚 Is rule ki poori detail

**A. Verbs of covering / filling / loading / decorating — pattern: `verb + object + WITH + substance`**

- splash, spray, sprinkle, smear, cover, fill, load, decorate, paint, stuff, cram, furnish, present, provide, supply, threaten, blame… *(kuch verbs dono patterns lete hain)*

✔ *She splashed the wall with paint.*
✘ *She splashed the wall from paint.*

✔ *Spray the plants with water.*
✔ *Fill the glass with milk.*
✔ *The truck was loaded with goods.*
✔ *The room was decorated with flowers.*

**B. Do valid patterns (dono sahi) — "with" vs "on/into"**
- `splash/spray/sprinkle something ON something` → *She splashed paint **on** the wall.*
- `splash/spray/sprinkle something WITH something` → *She splashed the wall **with** paint.*
Yahan **subject–object ka order badalne** par preposition badal jaata hai. Galti tab hoti hai jab in dono ko mix kar diya jaaye: *splashed the wall **from** paint* ✘.

**C. "FROM" kab use karein?** Source / origin / separation / reason:

✔ *She comes **from** Japan.* (origin)
✔ *He suffers **from** fever.* (reason)
✔ *The thief was saved **from** the police.* (separation)
✔ *Prevented him **from** going.* (from + V-ing)

**D. Exceptions / dhyan rakhne wali baat**
- **Made of** (material dikhta hai) vs **made from** (material dikhta nahi): *table is made of wood*, *wine is made from grapes*.
- **Made with** = kis cheez ko mila kar banaya (ingredient/means): *made with love*, *biryani made with basmati rice*.
- **Die of** (disease) / **die from** (reason/injury) — dono standard.
- Instrument: **with** a pen / a knife; Agent (karta): **by** Ram. *(Written **with** a pen **by** Ram.)*

---

## 🎯 SSC mein isi topic se aur kya aata hai

1. **Busy + V-ing:** ✘ *He was busy to read.* ✔ *He was busy reading.* (busy ke baad preposition/gerund)
2. **Cover/Fill/Load + with:** ✘ *The box was filled by chocolates.* ✔ *filled **with** chocolates.*
3. **by vs with:** ✘ *The letter was written **by** a pen.* ✔ *written **with** a pen **by** me.*
4. **Since vs From:** ✘ *I am working here **from** 2010.* ✔ *I have been working here **since** 2010.* (`from 2010 to 2015` — timeline ke liye sahi)
5. **Prevented from + V-ing:** ✘ *He was prevented to go.* ✔ *prevented **from** going.*
6. **Suffer from / Afraid of / Accused of / Deprived of:** ✘ *He is afraid **from** dogs.* ✔ *afraid **of** dogs.*
7. **Written / Spoken to / Married to:** ✘ *She is married **with** him.* ✔ *married **to** him.*
8. **of vs off:** ✘ *made **off** wood.* ✔ *made **of** wood; fell **off** the bike.*
9. **Differ from (person) / differ with (opinion):** ✘ *I differ **with** you in looks.* ✔ *differ **from** you in looks.*
10. **Give / Provide / Supply — with:** ✔ *Provided me **with** books* / *provided me books* (dono chalte hain), par *provided **from*** ✘.

---

## 🧠 Yaad rakhne ki trick

> **"Bharo–poto–chhidko" = WITH.** (Fill it **with** water, cover it **with** paint, splash it **with** colours.)
> **"Kahan se aaya" = FROM.** (Came **from** Japan, saved **from** danger.)
> Urdu/Hindi trick: *"se"* do matlab rakhta hai — *maadhyam se* (**with**) aur *srot se* (**from**). Yahan *colours se chhidka* = maadhyam → **with**.

---

## 📝 Ek line mein revision
**Cover/fill/splash/load/decorate jaise verbs ke saath material ke liye "with" aata hai, "from" nahi — isliye "from colours" galat hai, sahi hai "with colours".**
